# Run-level RTL native controls

Original manually authored OPC/XML generated by tools/rtl_run_fixture.py.
No corpus content is copied. The reference application exported the three-page native.pdf
with tools/export-reference.ps1. All three native pages were inspected.
The source passes the supplied OOXML schema checks.

Twenty-one cases cross Latin, European digits, Arabic-Indic digits, Hebrew,
Arabic, mixed Latin/Hebrew/numbers and a single Arabic-Indic zero with explicit
RTL false, RTL true and RTL true plus complex-script formatting. The latter
uses Courier New, 16pt, bold and italic; ordinary formatting is Arial 10pt.
Each tested run sits between independent LTR Left/Right text runs.

ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 17.3.2.30 (rtl), 17.3.2.7 (cs), 17.3.2.2 (bCs),
17.3.2.17 (iCs) and 17.3.2.39 (szCs) specify direction hints and complex-script
formatting. The specification leaves rtl=true on strong LTR text and rtl=false
on strong RTL text unspecified; these cases record native compatibility behavior,
not a claimed contradiction of a defined specification rule.

The reference application keeps ABC def in logical order under RTL but changes the complex-script
formatting when those overrides are present. RTL reverses the order of European
number groups separated by whitespace; mixed Hebrew/Latin/numeric text also
reorders. The Arabic-Indic zero uses complex-script formatting under RTL.
These observations rule out simply dropping the import guard or reversing all
characters. Full layout, caret/hit-testing and serialization need verification.

record_rtl_run_reference.py independently records every native glyph origin,
font, size and weight, and binds source/PDF/case hashes. This is native evidence,
not an implementation test pass. The engine still rejects RTL runs. Additional
controls may be needed for wrapping, style inheritance and editing boundaries.
